system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Positions

| ID | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general warranty cap. The 20% fallback may be used only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft; none has been given. | **Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6m** — the matching fallback figure is not authorised merely because Seller proposed it. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** tipping basket, with Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal materially reduces recovery through higher thresholds and a deductible basket. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**. | **24 months after Completion**; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given. | **Counter at 24 months** — the unauthorised fallback should not displace the Buyer’s baseline. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same general cap and time limit for “administrative simplicity.” | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject and insert a separate regime** — ownership, authority and capacity risks cannot be diluted by general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to **all Claims of any nature**; no adequate express fraud carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance**, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insist on the full carve-out** — this is a mandatory Buyer position and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. | Only **specific, fair disclosure** identifying the relevant warranty and sufficient detail to understand the nature and scope of the matter; no deemed disclosure through the whole data room, registers or prudent searches. | **Delete general disclosure and require specific disclosure** — document availability alone does not fairly disclose a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier must be narrow and use identified knowledge persons and an appropriate reasonable-enquiry standard, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject and narrowly redraft, if retained at all** — constructive and adviser-wide knowledge improperly transfers diligence risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied is disclosed. | Before Completion, obtain **effective consent** and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied; it must be a genuine condition precedent, not consent-on-delivery. | **Strengthen the condition precedent and prohibit waiver without Buyer control** — Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m/30% of FY26 revenue and the present record is incomplete. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release will be provided after Completion. | Current payout statement, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject an unsecured post-Completion release mechanic** — Buyer must not acquire the Company while Riverlark debt or security remains outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** Completion bonuses are said to be Seller’s matter but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are not addressed. | Express line item or Seller funding for the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with clear treatment in the funds flow. | **Revise the funds flow and allocate all amounts to Seller** — silence risks the Company, and therefore Buyer, funding Seller-triggered Completion costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; Seller regards it as adequate. DD-010 records **AUD 180,000 open**, but this is not independently verified, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Broader indemnity covering failure to obtain ownership/transfer of relevant Project Materials and resulting loss, costs and third-party exposure, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify payment/assignment status** — the narrow payment indemnity does not fully protect against defective IP ownership, and the AUD 180,000 remains unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure does not establish access, exact scope, notification duty, breach or loss. | Preservation of logs and evidence, prompt investigation, ongoing written updates, Buyer consultation/control over material notifications and remediation, and appropriate warranty/covenant protection—without assuming a confirmed breach or loss amount. | **Add investigation and preservation obligations while reserving liability treatment** — the facts remain incomplete, so neither dismissal nor a quantified claim is justified. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability; do not automatically treat them as Debt or deduct them from price. | **Reserve position pending diligence and specific contractual analysis** — the disclosure does not establish that the renewals are ordinary-course, unavoidable, accrued or terminable. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller proposes general limitations for all Claims and regards Tax/IP as settled under that regime. | Distinct regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, with no hidden override by general limitations. | **Reject the universal general-regime override and add express precedence language** — different risks require deliberately negotiated caps, periods and exclusions. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on the internal Company share register at DD-012 as evidence that Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, valid issue, encumbrance-free title, authority and ability to transfer, supported by original/certified corporate records, searches, releases and Completion deliverables. | **Require independent verification and title deliverables** — DD-012 identifies Seller’s internal source but is not independent proof of good, unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller asserts that Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the proposed general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms expressly **open** pending negotiation and diligence; assume neither unlimited liability nor any agreed resolution. | **Reject the assertion of settlement and reserve all rights** — a counterparty statement cannot create agreement or authority, and the applicable risk allocation remains unresolved. |
=== END ADVICE ===
